target.title: perf(gateway): use predicate-first listing for tasks.list to avoid full-registry clone+sort
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #101716 — the `tasks.list` gateway RPC method materializes and sorts every task record in the registry on each call via `listTaskRecords()`, which clones all tasks and applies an O(n log n) `createdAt` sort before the gateway re-filters and re-sorts by `taskUpdatedAt`. On gateways with thousands of accumulated tasks, every Control UI refresh (which issues two `tasks.list` calls) allocates a full clone array, causing:

- **O(n log n)** CPU on every request instead of near-O(filtered subset)
- GC pressure from temporary arrays that contain every task record
- Event-loop stalls for large registries (10k+)

## Why This Change Was Made

Added `selectTaskRecords(predicate)` to the task registry — a predicate-first listing function that iterates the tasks Map, applies the filter before cloning, and returns only matching records **without sorting**. The gateway `tasks.list` handler now uses this instead of `listTaskRecords()`, so:

- Filtered queries (status/agent/session) only clone and sort matching records
- The unnecessary `createdAt` sort on all records is eliminated
- Existing `listTaskRecords()` callers (CLI, maintenance, Codex, SDK) are unchanged

## User Impact

- Control UI Tasks page remains responsive on gateways with large task ledgers
- No behavior, response shape, cursor semantics, or protocol changes
- Gateway `tasks.list` ordering and pagination are identical

## Evidence

- `pnpm test src/gateway/server-methods/tasks.test.ts` — 12 tests passed (2 files)
- `pnpm test src/tasks/task-registry.test.ts` — 107 tests passed
- `git diff --check` — clean
